zotero.abstractNote: Synaptic plasticity rules are fundamental to learning and memory in the brain. However, identifying these rules from experimental data is challenging because different plasticity mechanisms can potentially lead to similar network-level dynamics. Here, we investigate this degeneracy of plasticity rules by using simulation-based inference to identify families of rules that produce indistinguishable network dynamics. We find that a wide range of plasticity rules can generate the same network activity, and that these rules can be distinguished by their dependence on pre- and post-synaptic activity. Our results suggest that degeneracy is a fundamental property of plasticity rules, and that experimental approaches must be designed to account for this redundancy.
